title: Piano parts and keyboard with guitar
summary: His piano parts are fully written for school bands; he avoids piano and guitar together except Basie and Freddie Green.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What do your piano parts look like?

Well they’re extremely well written. Because that’s the discipline you get for writing for publishing. You know everything has to be written out. But now for my own recordings or for a professional band I’ll only give certain things that I definitely want to have, and the rest is them because they, I mean anybody can write a better piano part than I can, but I can get the basic one down there. So when you’re writing for school bands, colleges and high school, everything has to be written out, the bass line, the piano part. Now they can ignore that if they have the chops and the skills, but everything is written out. So my piano parts are very, very well written.
Do you like to have keyboard and guitar in your own groups?
No. No. They get in the way of each other. Although I will hand guitar on two pieces on my new recording as melodic instruments, not as a part of the rhythm section.

Yeah I don’t know, I mean Basie and Freddie Green is probably about it. I mean I don’t know anybody else that can pull that off. But then they had their roles to play you know. Because Basie would just tinkle and Freddie would keep it going.
